title: Fix undercounting of streaming prefix tokens in per-model usage charts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Symptom: Per-model daily token totals for streaming endpoints are showing a persistent ~3-7% undercount versus raw event logs for several customers using streaming previews. The undercount is most obvious in models with long-lived streaming sessions (prefix-heavy workloads) and during high-burst periods. The Console charts (per-model breakdown) show a gap that is later partially corrected by a manual backfill run but discrepancies remain. Impact: billing and quota usage visibility are inaccurate; customers experience unexpected quota exhaustion or incorrect cost attributions.

This ticket owns diagnosis, fix, and reconciliation for the streaming-prefix undercount and the related backfill correctness gaps. The fix must be safe for production (can be rolled out incrementally) and must include monitoring to detect regressions.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create a long-running streaming session against streaming endpoint model: example app that streams partial completions frequently (every ~2-4 tokens).
2) Run sustained load for several hours with batching enabled on the runtime and with autoscaling events triggered, to replicate merge operations on streaming deltas.
3) Compare per-model daily totals in Console -> Per-model usage to raw event logs (s3/clickhouse/raw_events table) aggregated by stream_id; observe ~3-7% lower total in Console for affected models.
4) Trigger a manual backfill of streaming deltas and observe a partial uplift in Console totals, but not full reconciliation for sessions where delta merging lost interim events.
root_cause: When streaming clients emit frequent interim token-delta events, the ingestion pipeline's batch-merge logic collapses adjacent partial-delta events into a single summary if they are processed in the same ingestion batch. Due to a bug in the merge key (we used model+customer+approx_ts instead of persistent stream_id+seq), interim deltas from the same stream were deduplicated incorrectly, dropping token counts. Additionally, the backfill job only replays final commit events and the raw-event retention query did not include the streaming interim index, so historical reconciliation missed those dropped deltas. Edge factors: autoscaling-induced re-sharding and our rate-limiter fallbacks sometimes produced events attributed to fallback-model variants, further misattributing tokens in per-model breakdowns.
proposed_solution: 1) Fix ingestion merge key to include canonical stream_id and sequence number so interim deltas are accumulated instead of deduplicated.
2) Update real-time aggregator to retain a small in-memory per-stream accumulator for >2s sessions to avoid collapsing adjacent deltas across micro-batches during high-throughput windows.

3) Extend backfill job to scan raw stream-event index (raw_events_streaming_delta) with seq ordering and regenerate per-stream cumulative tokens, producing corrective delta events that ingestion can apply idempotently.
4) Add attribution rule to reassign tokens that were recorded against fallback-model variants back to the pinned model when stream metadata contains original_model_id.
5) Add integration tests and a canary rollout plan gated by synthetic traffic comparisons to raw logs.
6) Update Console charts to show a "backfilled correction" annotation and an option to toggle including backfilled adjustments in the timeline.
7) Run historical reconciliation for the past 90 days for models with high streaming traffic and run a phased customer notification for any billing-impacting corrections >1%.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end synthetic test: for a controlled streaming session with known tokens, Console per-model total matches raw event aggregation within +/- 0.1%.
2) Daily production diff between Console and raw_events_streaming aggregation reduced to <0.3% for the top 20 streaming models over a 7-day window post-rollout.
3) Backfill job produces idempotent corrective events and a verification report listing corrected models and percent deltas; corrections >1% must surface to Billing runbook for manual review.
4) Monitoring alert (SLO) firing if per-model diff rises above 1% for more than 2 hours after rollout; dashboard panels added for quick triage.
5) No user-visible incidents caused by the canary rollout (errors <0.1% increase in ingestion error rate, latency increase <5%).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): deploy ingestion keyfix + in-memory accumulator to 2% of ingestion fleet; run synthetic streaming traffic for 24h and compare per-model totals.
Phase 1 (expanded): deploy to 25% with backfill disabled; run metric comparisons and verify stability for 48h.
Phase 2 (backfill dry-run): enable backfill job in dry-run mode (generate corrective events but do not apply) for 24h and compare expected corrections with observed gaps.
Phase 3 (apply): enable corrective backfill gradually by model cohort (low-risk customers first) and monitor billing diffs and customer tickets channel.
Phase 4 (cleanup): once stable, run 90-day reconciliation window and publish reconciliation report and billing adjustments per billing policy.
monitoring_queries: ClickHouse: SELECT model_id, toDate(event_ts) as day, sum(token_count) as raw_tokens FROM raw_events_streaming_delta WHERE event_type='delta' GROUP BY model_id, day ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 50;
ConsoleAggregate: SELECT model_id, day, console_tokens FROM per_model_daily_aggregates WHERE day >= today()-7 ORDER BY model_id;

DiffQuery: SELECT a.model_id, a.day, a.raw_tokens, b.console_tokens, (a.raw_tokens - b.console_tokens)/a.raw_tokens as pct_diff FROM (raw_events_streaming_delta agg) a JOIN (per_model_daily_aggregates) b USING (model_id, day) WHERE a.raw_tokens > 1000 ORDER BY pct_diff DESC LIMIT 200;
Alert: pct_diff > 0.01 for any model for >2 hours -> fire pager and post to #usage-accuracy channel.
